text:
This looks like September 2020. Unemployment is 8.4%, which matches August 2020, and the 10-year yield is 0.66%. The fed funds rate is 0.09%, and the VIX at 26 fits early September 2020, after the selloff. US equity returned -3.7% over the month, which suggests September rather than August (in August 2020 equities were up).

Unemployment of 8.4% was the August 2020 reading, published in early September. So the snapshot could be end of August or end of September, but August equities were strongly up (+7%). September 2020 had a -3.7% S&P total return, which fits. The September unemployment rate was 7.9%, though, so the latest published value would be 8.4% only if the September jobs report had not yet come out, and at the end of September it had not (it came out Oct 2). That fits.

Core CPI at 1.73% matches August 2020. Industrial production at -7.73% YoY matches August 2020. Gold fell 4.2% in September, which also fits.
